detailedDescription.problem:
Conformance problems in SDTM and SEND data are usually found late, when the
finished datasets are run through a separate validation tool shortly before
submission. Fixing them then means going back through programs that were
written weeks earlier. Programmers working in R have had no way to run
CDISC's conformance rules from inside the session where they build the data.
detailedDescription.solution:
coreval is an R package that runs the CDISC Open Rules on a data frame or on
a whole study folder, offline, with no API key. A programmer can check a
dataset right after writing the code that builds it. Each finding names the
rule, the record and the values involved, and results can be filtered and
written to Excel together with the rules that could not be evaluated and the
reason. The rules are shipped as data taken from a pinned commit of
cdisc-open-rules, and that commit is recorded in every findings file.

It complements CDISC's rules engine rather than replacing it: coreval is a
first check while programming, not a replacement for a validated tool.
To test its results, coreval was run on CDISC's pilot submission
(22 datasets, 294,677 records) and every finding was compared rule by rule
with the reference engine. Rules are also run against the example data
CDISC publishes for them, and coverage is documented:
https://github.com/hrach-gevorgyan/coreval/blob/master/docs/REAL-STUDY.md
https://github.com/hrach-gevorgyan/coreval/blob/master/docs/COVERAGE.md
detailedDescription.openSourceConsiderations:
Conformance checking should be open to every programmer, including those
at small companies and in academia. Publishing it as open source lets users
inspect exactly how each rule is evaluated, report disagreements, and adopt
it without licensing barriers. The CDISC material it uses is itself MIT
licensed, and its origin is documented in the package (inst/COPYRIGHTS).
detailedDescription.maintenanceModel:
Issues are reported on GitHub
(https://github.com/hrach-gevorgyan/coreval/issues). The package is
released on CRAN with semantic versioning, and every change is recorded in
NEWS.md. Each push is checked on Windows, macOS and Linux through GitHub
Actions, and the main branch is protected. When CDISC updates the Open
Rules, the pinned commit is updated, the conformance tests are re-run, and
changes in results are reviewed before release.
detailedDescription.projectSize:
Medium (M). About 10,000 lines of R code evaluating 1,054 bundled rules
through a general set of operators, with a test suite, a conformance test
harness and a real-study comparison. Developed and maintained by one person.
detailedDescription.contributors:
Contributions are welcome through GitHub issues and pull requests, under
the MIT licence and the project's code of conduct. No contributor licence
agreement is required.
detailedDescription.userDetails:
Working knowledge of SDTM or SEND and basic R. The getting-started guide
and function reference are on the website:
https://hrach-gevorgyan.github.io/coreval/
detailedDescription.preRequisites:
R 4.1 or later on Windows, macOS or Linux. Installed from CRAN with
install.packages("coreval"). Required packages are data.table and haven;
a few optional packages add specific formats, such as Excel export.
No network access or API key is needed.
detailedDescription.projectServiceOptions:
No paid services are offered. The MIT licence allows any company to
provide support, validation or integration services around the package.
detailedDescription.goalsObjectives:
Keep the bundled rules in step with CDISC's published Open Rules releases.
Add ADaM once CDISC publishes CORE conformance rules for ADaM. Widen
coverage of areas the current test data exercises least, such as split
domains and define.xml driven rules. Make coreval part of the pharmaverse
set of R packages (a request is under review).
detailedDescription.communications:
Release notes in NEWS.md and GitHub releases, the package website, and
announcements on LinkedIn and R community channels (R Weekly, Posit
Community). The package has been submitted for inclusion in pharmaverse.
detailedDescription.additionalInformation:
coreval is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed
by CDISC. Happy to answer any questions by email.
